title: Architect-declared operation arithmetic
description: Select a supported exact arithmetic profile, or explicitly delegate unsupported semantics. Type and dimension names reference the existing architecture contract.

product_data_type.description: Declared integer data type wide enough for an exact product.

post_operations.description: A DAG of named post-reduction stages, not a fixed order. Each stage names exactly one predecessor via depends_on -- either the literal string 'accumulator' or another stage's key -- so execution order is derived by following depends_on edges back from post_output, not by object-key order. Empty object means no post-processing at all (post_output must then be 'accumulator'). The current integer GEMM backend supports at most one each of bias_add, wrap, relu, and affine_quantize, in any order the depends_on chain expresses, plus any number of llm_defined stages (each with its own closed-grammar formula -- see formula.py) for a post-op this tool has no other built-in kind for.

scale_multiplier.description: Positive numerator of the fixed-point affine scale.

scale_shift.description: Power-of-two denominator: effective scale is scale_multiplier / 2^scale_shift.

formula.description: A closed-grammar expression over the single free variable 'value' (the running scalar entering this stage): integer literals, + - * and unary -, comparisons (< <= > >= == !=), and calls to min/max (2 args), abs (1 arg), clip(x, lo, hi) (3 args). No division, modulo, bitwise ops, exponentiation, attribute access, subscripting, other names, or other calls. See pool/operation_metadata/formula.py for the exact grammar and its rationale.

post_output.description: The stage (key in post_operations) or the literal 'accumulator' whose output feeds result_conversion.

reason.description: Name the unsupported mathematical behavior. Exact semantics remain in operations[].semantics; no code-owned arithmetic is inferred for this profile.

extension_request.description: Optional exact link to the operation-domain verification_extensions request that owns this unsupported arithmetic. Omitted only for legacy coarse llm_extension contracts.
